members.subject: civil-engineering-structural-engineering
members.question: Why should a structural free-body diagram be prepared before calculating reactions?
choices: It replaces the need to check units.
It proves the member is elastic.
It determines concrete strength directly.
It exposes supports, external actions, and sign conventions for the equilibrium equations.
members.answer: It exposes supports, external actions, and sign conventions for the equilibrium equations.
members.explanation: A free-body diagram isolates the selected structure and shows every external load, support reaction, location, and sign convention before the equilibrium equations are written. That lets the solver check force and moment balance without assuming symmetry or omitting a reaction; material strength and unit checks remain separate design checks.
